text:
Ben: Hi all, joining today. Trying to build the runtime from source on my work machine (Windows 11 + WSL2). Followed the README, using the docker dev image `redwood/dev:cuda-12.1` but the link step fails. Any quick pointers?

Ben: build output: 
```
[ 34%] Linking CXX executable llm_server
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcudart_static
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
ptxas info    : 0 bytes gmem, 0 bytes cmem[0]
ptxas fatal   : LTO fatal error: symbol '___cudaRegisterFatBinary' multiply defined
```

Ben: I'm running the container with `docker run --gpus all -v /mnt/c/Users/ben/dev:/src -w /src redwood/dev:cuda-12.1 make -j8`

Mika: welcome! :wave: WSL adds a few gotchas. First check if the container actually sees the GPU: run `docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi` and `nvidia-container-cli info`

Natanael: the `-lcudart_static` missing is often from mixing static/dynamic CUDA runtimes. Are you binding host CUDA dirs into the container (e.g., /usr/local/cuda)? That can produce conflicting headers/libs between host and image.

Rosie: on WSL specifically, make sure you have the latest NVIDIA WSL driver on Windows (not just in WSL). Windows driver exposes the GPU to WSL, but if the host driver is older than the toolkit in the image you'll get missing symbols. `nvidia-smi` on the Windows host vs inside container can tell you which driver is actually used.

Ben: I didn't bind /usr/local/cuda. I do see `nvidia-smi` in the container returns a GPU, driver 510.47, and `nvcc --version` shows CUDA 12.1.

Mika: driver 510 is too old for CUDA 12.1 (needs ~525+). Two choices: use a dev image matching your driver (we have `redwood/dev:cuda-11.8`), or update the Windows WSL NVIDIA driver. If you update, reboot Windows and update the WSL kernel (wsl --update).

Natanael: the LTO / multiply defined symbol often comes from linking both static and shared cudart (e.g., -lcudart and -lcudart_static). Check CMake flags: remove `-static` variants or prefer `-lcudart` dynamic. Also check `CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS` for stray -Wl,--whole-archive patterns.

Rosie: another WSL tip: avoid mounting the repo via DrvFs into the container for heavy builds (`/mnt/c/...`) — filewatching and build tools are slower; prefer working inside the WSL filesystem (~/dev) and bind that to the container. Not strictly a linker fix, but speeds iteration.

Ben: ok trying two experiments: 1) switch to `redwood/dev:cuda-11.8` image and rebuild; 2) check CMakeLinker flags for static cudart.

Ben: quick follow-up — switching to 11.8 image made the `-lcudart_static` error go away, but I'm now hitting `undefined reference to cuGetProcAddress`.

Mika: that undefined reference smells like newer APIs called by some third-party lib built against 12.x. Do a `ldd` on the failing object/binary to see which libCUDA or libnvidia is picked. Also grep the build dir for `cuGetProcAddress` to locate the object using it.

Natanael: if a dependency (e.g., cuBLAS or a custom plugin) was compiled against 12.x, you'll need to rebuild it against 11.8 or use the matching container. For onboarding, I recommend starting with the 11.8 image for folks on older laptops. We'll track common laptop+image combos in the checklist.

Rosie: tagging infra for WSL driver guidance if folks need help updating Windows drivers.

infra-bot: INFRA-427 created: "WSL driver guidance + add dev image compatibility matrix to onboarding". Assigned to infra oncall.

Ben: thanks everyone — I'll keep iterating and post results. Adding notes to the onboarding doc once I confirm the exact combo that worked. :thumbsup:
